title: Vector Arithmetic and Cosine Similarity in a Toy Embedding Space
description: Compute emb["king"] - emb["man"] + emb["woman"] and find which word vector in emb has the highest cosine similarity to the result.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `numpy as np` and define a 4-word dictionary `emb` that maps `"king"`, `"queen"`, `"man"`, and `"woman"` to 2D NumPy vectors.
Compute `analogy = emb["king"] - emb["man"] + emb["woman"]`, calculate the cosine similarity between `analogy` and every vector in `emb`, and print the word with the highest similarity.

Look at lines 10-11: vector subtraction and addition run coordinate by coordinate on line 10. Line 11 divides the dot product `v @ analogy` by the product of the two vector norms to get cosine similarity.

steps.question: What 2D vector does `emb["king"] - emb["man"] + emb["woman"]` produce on line 10, and which word in `emb` has cosine similarity `1.0` with it?
steps.answer: `[0.9, 0.8] - [0.1, 0.8] + [0.1, 0.2]` equals `[0.9, 0.2]`, which is identical to `emb["queen"]`, giving `"queen"` a cosine similarity of `1.0`.

steps.description: After computing all four cosine similarities, `max(sims, key=sims.get)` selects `queen` with cosine similarity `1.0`.
